parts: Given access, an assistant can open, change and delete files, send messages and reach connected systems. The account it borrows decides how far it reaches.
Left running alone, it continues past its first mistake. A wrong instruction repeated quickly is harder to undo than a wrong sentence.
Decide in advance which actions need confirmation, which information stays out, and who is able to stop a run that has started.

items.text: A labelled AI demonstration is played here in the room: a familiar face and a familiar voice saying words that were never spoken. The recording is not published. Permission from BBT covers the room only.
The point it makes: a recognisable face and a recognisable voice do not by themselves establish where the words came from. The next slide shows what can be done about that.

parts: A digital profile for each file
Record each original’s source details and file hash. BBT Archive can digitally sign the record. A checking tool then compares the hash and verifies the signature.
AI finds exact passages and context in BBT Archive. A quotation absent after a full check is suspect. Voice similarity alone cannot authenticate a recording.

Before we ask whether an “ask Prabhupāda” service answers accurately, we must ask whether it should exist. A synthesised reply in his person is not his instruction, and devotees may not hear the difference.
Content ID matches reused recordings. Rights holders can pursue infringements. EU rules require disclosure of covered deepfakes.

items.text: Approved tools should cite the Archive and separate quotation from summary. Whether a personified tool is permitted at all is a decision of its own.

parts: A finished chapter from a human translator, with normal editorial work. The defined checks run afterwards, never instead.
Findings are ordered by severity. The editor accepts or rejects each one, and the confirmed errors are fewer.
A Bulgarian hyphenation dictionary. By hand, two hours a day for three years. With these checks, two hours a day for three weeks.
His Guru Mahārāja called the printing press the bṛhad-mṛdaṅga, the great drum. He dictated these books into a machine. The tools changed; the responsibility did not.

items.text: A prepared demo collection. 50 files with about 23 million words, prepared for this demonstration. The manifest describes this collection’s scope.
One question, asked precisely. “What did he say about children” returns a thousand statements. A defined question returns a passage we can open and read.
References we can inspect. Open the cited verse, letter or transcript. Read the surrounding passage and distinguish quotations from the model’s summary.
This demo illustrates source checking. BBT Archive remains the reference.
The corpus manifest
Ordered in 1995. A 1995 GBC resolution called for a consolidated Law Book. This demonstration uses the 2018 edition as its starting point.
Assembled overnight. Published resolutions from 2019 to 2026 organised under the book’s chapters, with references to the source documents.
A draft, and nothing more. An unapproved working draft. An authorised committee must review which provisions remain in force and resolve conflicts.
422 pages with search and source links. Legal and institutional review still matter.

parts: Bhakti-śāstrī and higher qualifications depend on students’ understanding. An essay alone may not establish who wrote it.
Smooth prose, repeated phrasing and reading aloud can raise questions. AI can also imitate an uneven style and deliberate mistakes.
Pangram and GPTZero can flag text. False positives and missed AI text occur. A score or a hidden prompt is insufficient evidence.
Oral defence, drafts and supervised work help assess understanding. Course leaders should define allowed AI use and disclosure.

items.text: Where is the line for our own courses, and who draws it?

parts: A subscription buys capacity, and capacity invites more hours. Morning programme, japa and rest are the first things those hours take.
The work moves into the head
Less mechanical work, more specifying, judging and checking. That is a heavier kind of tiredness and it is easy to miss in ourselves.
Companion applications answer warmly at any hour, and the young are most exposed. Providers added protections after serious cases; the pull remains.

items.text: We care for devotees. Their attention and their daily sādhana are part of that care.
1. Image, voice and likeness: May anyone generate the image, voice or video of Śrīla Prabhupāda, or of a devotee? Should a tool that answers in his person exist at all?
2. Our education: Is AI usage permitted in essays and examinations, and to what extent?
3. Research: How far may AI go in the studies and surveys we commission?
4. Devotee data: What must never be entered into a public tool?
5. Policy ownership: Which policies already exist globally, in Europe and in each yatra? Who is responsible for the gaps?
6. Accountability: Who is responsible when AI goes wrong in ISKCON's name?
These questions need named owners and an agreed process for decisions.
ELM asks the RGB to begin work on an AI policy for Europe.
